research_text:
# Research brief

## 1. API and finding

`javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec` specifies two parameters for a GCM `Cipher`: the IV bytes and the authentication-tag length in **bits**. Its constructors accept either the entire `src` byte array or a slice specified by `offset` and `len`; they copy the IV material. Other inputs, including the key and additional authenticated data (AAD), are handled by `Cipher`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html))

The reported finding concerns the **`src` IV-source argument at one of those constructor events**. The rule requires `randomized[src]`. Its text does not define what evidence establishes that predicate, so the finding alone does not establish the IV’s runtime origin or its uniqueness across encryptions. The rule also does not model cipher initialization or encryption events. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/GCMParameterSpec.crysl))

Source: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html`

## 2. Documented usage and remediation guidance

- **IV lifecycle:** Oracle says GCM encryption requires IV uniqueness for a given key and recommends reinitializing the `Cipher` with a different IV after each encryption operation. Merely changing a transformation does not address reuse of an initialized cipher’s key/IV combination. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html))
- **IV construction:** NIST SP 800-38D documents both deterministic and random-bit-generator-based constructions, subject to their respective requirements. Its RBG-based construction has invocation limits; randomness alone is not a guarantee of uniqueness. Thus the CrySL randomization predicate is narrower than NIST’s documented construction choices. ([nvlpubs.nist.gov](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/legacy/sp/nistspecialpublication800-38d.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Authentication:** Oracle documents that AAD, if used, must be supplied before ciphertext processing; the tag is appended during encryption and verified during decryption. A tag mismatch is reported as `AEADBadTagException`. The JCA example uses the same GCM parameters and AAD for decryption. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/14/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html?utm_source=openai))
- **Tag length:** Oracle lists 96, 104, 112, 120 and 128 bits, and 32 or 64 bits for certain applications; it cautions that providers may not support every value accepted by the specification object. The CrySL rule accepts only the first five. NIST has announced a revision intended to remove support for tags shorter than 96 bits; that announcement is not itself the revised standard. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html))

The documentation’s prospective remedy for IV reuse is to use a different IV for each encryption under the key and reinitialize the cipher accordingly. The sources do **not** prescribe a repository-specific fix or an automatic repair for existing ciphertext.

Sources: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html` and `https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/legacy/sp/nistspecialpublication800-38d.pdf`

## 3. Compatibility and migration

- **Persisted and wire data:** The API specifies parameters, not an application’s storage or wire framing. Decryption requires the corresponding GCM parameters and AAD; changing how new IVs are generated does not by itself provide those values for old data. Oracle documents that the tag is appended to ciphertext, but does not prescribe a universal IV-storage format or a versioned migration path. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/security/crypto/CryptoSpec.html))
- **Platform support:** Oracle marks `GCMParameterSpec` as available since Java **1.7**. Android documents the class and both constructors from **API level 19**. Class availability does not establish that every provider supports every desired tag length or configuration. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html))
- **Unresolved:** The cited API documentation does not identify an existing application format, legacy-data migration procedure, or compatibility guarantee for a particular provider.

Android source: `https://developer.android.com/reference/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec`

## 4. Exact CrySL rule

The supplied rule file declares `SPEC javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec`. Its matching and randomization clauses are, verbatim:

```text
c1: GCMParameterSpec(tagLen, src);
c2: GCMParameterSpec(tagLen, src, offset, len);
Con := c1 | c2;
```

```text
randomized[src];
```

The rule names the `GCMParameterSpec` constructor events of the specified class, with respectively **two and four arguments**. The declared argument types are `(int, byte[])` and `(int, byte[], int, int)`. **No:** the rule does not state a name-only match for a method on an unrelated receiver type. It specifies the class and these argument lists; it does not itself describe the detector’s implementation of method resolution or inheritance. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/GCMParameterSpec.crysl))

It requires `randomized[src]` and also states these global constraints: tag length is one of 96, 104, 112, 120 or 128; `length[src] >= offset + len`; `offset >= 0`; and `len > 0`. The two-argument event does not bind `offset` or `len`, and the rule text does not explain how those global constraints are evaluated for that event. It declares `preparedGCM[this]` under `ENSURES` but does not define that predicate’s consumption. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/GCMParameterSpec.crysl))

**Source limitation:** the URL points to the moving `master` branch. The supplied SHA-256 was not independently verified in this research pass.

Rule source: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/GCMParameterSpec.crysl`
